differences.title: 1. CONSENSUS MECHANISM
differences.leftDesc: Raft uses a single leader elected by a majority. All decisions flow through the leader, simplifying state management and understanding.
differences.rightDesc: Paxos avoids a single leader. Proposers and acceptors achieve consensus through multiple rounds of proposals and promises, making it more complex.

differences.title: 2. COMPLEXITY
differences.leftDesc: Raft was designed for understandability, breaking consensus into distinct steps: leader election, log replication, and safety.
differences.rightDesc: Paxos is notoriously difficult due to its intricate proposal and acceptance phases, often leading to subtle implementation errors.

differences.title: 3. LEADER ELECTION
differences.leftDesc: Raft has a well-defined leader election process involving timeouts and vote requests to ensure a stable leader emerges.
differences.rightDesc: Paxos does not have an explicit leader election; agreement on a chosen leader emerges implicitly from successful proposals.

differences.title: 4. LOG REPLICATION
differences.leftDesc: In Raft, the elected leader dictates the log order and replicates entries to followers. This ensures consistency.

differences.title: 5. SAFETY GUARANTEES
differences.leftDesc: Raft ensures that once a log entry is committed, it will be applied to all state machines that have received it.
differences.rightDesc: Paxos guarantees that if a value is chosen, it is chosen uniquely, but ensuring a value is chosen can be complex.

differences.title: 6. PERFORMANCE
differences.leftDesc: Raft's leader-centric approach often leads to fewer communication rounds, resulting in higher throughput and lower latency.
differences.rightDesc: Paxos's multi-round consensus and potential for proposer contention can introduce higher latency and lower throughput.

differences.title: 7. PRACTICAL USAGE
differences.leftDesc: Raft is preferred in many modern distributed systems (e.g., etcd, Consul) due to its clarity and ease of implementation.
differences.rightDesc: Paxos is a theoretical foundation; actual implementations are rare due to its complexity, but it influenced many algorithms.
